name: Cellular Base-Station Ingest Nodes
description: The INGEST half of the cellular program (typed contracts 1.0: FlatBuffers only, no JSON and no base64). cell-tower-source is the REQUEST-scoped aggregate; this plugin holds the ingest-only decisions and REUSES cell-tower-source's parse and deconflict unchanged. ingest lane: mark_query (TimerTick -> $FSO) reads the durable $IRM resume mark, ingest_plan (TimerTick + $FSB -> HttpRequest whose CONTEXT is the $APR run contract and the $IRM job) plans ONE ranged chunk, ingest_meta (records + HttpResponse + resume $IRM -> IngestRequest, records, candidate $IRM, or a FlowNotice on 304) authors the storage attribution, publish_request (IngestResult + IngestRequest + $IRM -> $IRM for hostcap/storage-write, publication POST) advances the mark only on a verified store. Cache lane: cache_plan ($HTQ -> $FSO queries + $APR job, or the $HTQ forwarded) and cache_freshness ($APR + $FSB -> $APR decision, $DAV, $TBS records) answer an /aggregate read from the store. Tile lane: tile_plan ($HTQ -> $FSO queries + $APR jobs, or an $APR refusal), tile_meta and tile ($APR + $FSB -> $QRP decision + $QRP projection page) serve bounded Web Mercator XYZ tiles, z 0-18, per-tile mode by count (<=2048 points, <=4096 a deterministic sample, else a 16x16 density grid). Node CONFIG through plugin.getConfig (typed $PIV, ConfigEntry list). NO CAPABILITIES: http, storage and flatsql are the generic hostcap connector nodes.

sequentialJustification.detail: All methods are single-pass transforms over the frames the flow hands them: they format a query, a fetch descriptor, an attribution frame or a mark. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool and no fan-out inside the guest. This guest can never spawn a thread, so it compiles clang/wasi-sequential rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.displayName: Answer from the store, or pass the request through
methods.description: THE CACHE GATE (owner 2026-08-14: 'the cell towers should load almost instantaneously'). One $HTQ in, exactly ONE lane out: a /tiles path is forwarded verbatim on `tile`; any route other than the aggregate (/providers, /credentials/*), an unreadable envelope, or a body carrying REFRESH:true is forwarded verbatim on `passthrough` to cell-tower-source route; an /aggregate read is answered FROM THE STORE: `query` is the dataset's DEFAULT FlatSQL query (node CONFIG cell_cache_sql, default SELECT _data FROM TBS ORDER BY _rowid DESC LIMIT ?, the caller's LIMIT capped at cell_cache_max_rows bound as an int64), `mark_query` reads the newest $IRM resume marks, and `job` is the $APR run contract (ROUTE aggregate-cache, METHOD, PATH, ACCEPT, IF_NONE_MATCH, SELECTION the cache SQL, PARAMETERS LIMIT, maxRows, provider) for cache_freshness. Only plugin.getConfig (typed $PIV) is called; capabilities [].

methods.displayName: Answer the cached rows with their age
methods.description: THE HONEST HALF OF THE CACHE. The cached $TBS rows (the $FSB DATA reassembled, verbatim) go out on `records` beside a $DAV saying what they are and how fresh: no resume mark -> KNOWN false, AVAILABLE false, UNAVAILABLE_REASON NotPublished (instant AND empty, never presented as current); a mark whose object is read to its end -> FRESH; a mark mid-ingest -> FRESH false; result frames that are not $IRM -> FRESH false (freshness 'unavailable', no timestamp guessed). RECORD_COUNT / BYTE_COUNT count the stream, PUBLISHED_AT_MS is the mark's UPDATED_AT, BATCH_ID its last chunk's. The $APR job is passed on as the decision with RESPONSE_HEADERS x-sdn-cache, x-sdn-cache-freshness, x-sdn-cache-stale and x-sdn-cache-providers (providerId=..;nextOffset=..;totalBytes=..;chunkIndex=..;state=..). BATCHING: every single-stream input port refuses a surplus frame with error code "batched-input-frames" (the compiled flow runtime drains a node's queue port-blind; maxStreams is declarative only); $FSB ports carry the result chunks of one query and take every chunk.

methods.description: THE TILE ROUTER. /tiles/meta -> meta_mark_query + meta_job; /tiles/{z}/{x}/{y} -> rows_query (scoped by default to the tile's own Web Mercator rectangle: SELECT _data FROM <cell_tile_relation> WHERE LATITUDE >= ?1 AND LATITUDE <= ?2 AND LONGITUDE >= ?3 AND LONGITUDE <= ?4 ORDER BY _rowid DESC LIMIT ?5 with four float64 bounds and the int64 row budget cell_tile_max_rows (default 25000); an explicit cell_tile_sql is used verbatim with the budget as its one parameter and the job says scoped false) + tile_mark_query + tile_job ($APR ROUTE tile, PARAMETERS z, x, y, maxRows, scoped, provider). BOUNDS ARE REFUSED, NEVER CLAMPED: anything else under /tiles, z outside [0,18], x or y outside [0,2^z) or a non-canonical integer is an $APR STATUS 400 (ERROR_CODE tile-path / tile-bounds) on `refusal`, for foundation/http-respond respond. Exactly one lane emits. BATCHING: every single-stream input port refuses a surplus frame with error code "batched-input-frames" (the compiled flow runtime drains a node's queue port-blind; maxStreams is declarative only); $FSB ports carry the result chunks of one query and take every chunk.

methods.displayName: Declare the tile layer's capability envelope
methods.description: THE TILE LAYER'S CAPABILITY ENVELOPE as one $QRP projection row: scheme xyz, minZoom 0, maxZoom 18, threshold 2048, budget 4096, densityN 16, latClamp 85.05112878, tileUrlTemplate, deconfliction statement, dataset, epoch, records, stale, cacheState; the page header carries the same dataset block as STORED, AS_OF_MS and STALE. records and epoch come from the resume mark, never a COUNT over the store; an empty store answers cacheState empty, records 0 and the Unix-epoch sentinel. The decision is the $QRP Request for foundation/http-respond respond_query (REPRESENTATION from the job's ACCEPT, ETAG its IF_NONE_MATCH). BATCHING: every single-stream input port refuses a surplus frame with error code "batched-input-frames" (the compiled flow runtime drains a node's queue port-blind; maxStreams is declarative only); $FSB ports carry the result chunks of one query and take every chunk.

methods.description: ONE BOUNDED TILE, AND THE MODE IS THE SERVER'S. The stored rows are filtered to the tile by re-deriving each point's (x,y) with the client's formulas and 1e-9 epsilon. count <= 2048 ships every point; count <= 4096 a deterministic stride sample (stride ceil(count/2048)); above, a 16x16 density grid. The answer is a $QRP projection page: points mode COLUMNS LATITUDE, LONGITUDE (exact doubles), density mode COLUMNS lon, lat, count (each non-empty cell's south-west corner, exact, and its count). TOTAL_COUNT is the tile's TRUE population, SCANNED the positioned records read, PARTIAL true when the read hit the row budget or was not scoped to the tile, TRUNCATED true for a sampled tile, STORED / AS_OF_MS / STALE the dataset block from the resume mark, MESSAGE 'tile z/x/y mode .. cache .. scoped .. malformed ..'. An empty store answers an empty tile, never fabricated sites. BATCHING: every single-stream input port refuses a surplus frame with error code "batched-input-frames" (the compiled flow runtime drains a node's queue port-blind; maxStreams is declarative only); $FSB ports carry the result chunks of one query and take every chunk.

methods.description: Emits ONE ranged HttpRequest (GET cell_ingest_url, range bytes=<offset>-<offset+chunk-1>, chunk cell_ingest_chunk_bytes clamped to 4 MiB because the Go host caps a response body there, TIMEOUT_MS cell_ingest_http_timeout_ms). Its CONTEXT is the run: a size-prefixed stream of the $APR run contract (ROUTE ingest, PARAMETERS PROVIDERS, METHOD, LIMIT, FULL_POPULATION true, provider, fetches 1; x-sdn-providers-consulted) and the $IRM job: this provider's newest stored mark (a mark of another provider is ignored; its decoder fields are dropped unless their DECODER_STATE_FORMAT is cell-tower-source/tinfl-v1, so a foreign blob is never resumed into) or a fresh mark at offset 0, with CHUNK_BYTE_BUDGET and MERGE_POLICY set. Emits nothing once the mark says the object is complete; fails closed (400 missing-ingest-url) without cell_ingest_url. BATCHING: every single-stream input port refuses a surplus frame with error code "batched-input-frames" (the compiled flow runtime drains a node's queue port-blind; maxStreams is declarative only); $FSB ports carry the result chunks of one query and take every chunk.

methods.displayName: Author the storage attribution for one chunk
methods.description: Reads the job from the HttpResponse's CONTEXT ($IRM), authors the IngestRequest the storage lane cannot invent (SCHEMA TBS.fbs, TAGS provider / cell_ingest_source_name / batch <provider>@<chunk offset> / source url, RECONCILE None because a batch is one CHUNK of the set, PROVENANCE from the response) and forwards the deconflicted records untouched. The candidate next mark ($IRM) goes to publish_request: NEXT_OFFSET is the decoder's own (from parse's `resume`, compressed lanes) or the end of the last COMPLETE row in the chunk (row-boundary correction); TOTAL_BYTES is Content-Range's denominator; the CSV header row is captured from chunk 0 only and only when it is text, and carried forward. HTTP 304 Not Modified is a successful fetch with nothing new: one FlowNotice Unchanged on `unchanged` and nothing else, so nothing is stored and the mark does not move. BATCHING: every single-stream input port refuses a surplus frame with error code "batched-input-frames" (the compiled flow runtime drains a node's queue port-blind; maxStreams is declarative only); $FSB ports carry the result chunks of one query and take every chunk.

methods.displayName: Advance the resume mark from the storage result
methods.description: Advances the resume mark FROM THE STORAGE RESULT, never at dispatch: the candidate $IRM becomes the durable one (RECORDS_COMMITTED + INSERTED, LAST_CHUNK RECORDS_STORED and COMMITTED_AT, UPDATED_AT, COMPLETED_AT when complete) on `mark_record`, for hostcap/storage-write. A REFUSED result (502 ingest-refused) and the silent nop - INSERTED 0 for a chunk that carried records (502 ingest-stored-nothing) - advance nothing. When cell_ingest_publish_url is set, `request` is the dataset-publication POST whose BODY is an IngestResult naming the batch; fail-closed otherwise. BATCHING: every single-stream input port refuses a surplus frame with error code "batched-input-frames" (the compiled flow runtime drains a node's queue port-blind; maxStreams is declarative only); $FSB ports carry the result chunks of one query and take every chunk.
